@@138546773 <p> The annual Pollinator Week is all about celebrating some of the smallest creatures that make the largest impact on the ecosystem . <p> The event , which ended Sunday , is celebrated internationally in support of pollinator health . Pollinating animals travel from plant to plant carrying pollen on their bodies that allows for the reproductive system of most flowering plants . Pollination is crucial to plant reproduction and the wider ecosystem that relies on plants as a food source . <p> " Birds , bats , bees , butterflies , beetles , and other small mammals that pollinate plants are responsible for bringing us one out of every three bites of food . They also sustain our ecosystems and produce our natural resources by helping plants reproduce , " according to the nonprofit Pollinator Partnership . <p> Around 87% of all flowering plants on Earth need help with pollination , including 75% of all food crops , according to Dr. Kelsey Fisher , assistant agricultural scientist with the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station . Pollinators provide pollination to over 180,000 different plant species and more than 1,200 crops vital @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ an important reminder of how critical pollinators are to the wider ecosystem and human food supply . But despite pollinators playing such a vital role , they remain vulnerable to pesticide use , parasites and disease , climate change and loss of habitat , Fisher said . <p> Rising temperatures are thought to be one of the main contributors to a decline in bumblebees . Numbers of North American bumblebees have fallen nearly 50% since 1974 . The biggest losses have occurred in places where temperatures have risen the highest , according to the U.S. Fish &amp; Wildlife Service . <p> " There 's a bunch of reasons why pollinators are in decline , but the one I like to focus on most , is creating suitable habitat for pollinators . We can talk about pesticide use , climate change or habitat loss . But the thing we personally have control over is what we put in our backyards . Our pollinators need different flowers that will bloom from May through October . Our lush beautiful green lawns do n't provide all of the resources that our pollinators need , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ lift and one thing we can take responsibility for is changing our landscaping . That way it helps lower that barrier and then we can start to work on things that are more abstract and bigger issues . The bigger thing is to have pollinator gardens or wild spaces . All of these practices can happen within balance . If there is a need for a grassy area in your yard , then by all means have that . But perhaps there is an area you can let grow wild or plant pollinators . I think creating even a small pollinator friendly habitat is key to their success . " <p> Some of the most important pollinator plants in Connecticut include bee balm , buttonbush , columbine , geranium , goldenrod , highbush blueberry , New England aster , New Jersey tea and swamp milkweed . Milkweed is the primary host plant for Monarch butterflies . <p> " These plants are often not at the big box store , they usually are sold at local nurseries , " Fisher said . " If your local nursery is not selling these @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ they can order them . I 've heard many times from people who asked and then found their nursery starting selling plants like milkweed or bee balm . So even if your local nursery does n't have these plants , always ask for them . " <p> While creating pollinator habitat is important in backyards , the state is also getting involved , and raising awareness about its designated pollinator sites scattered across several highway medians . <p> Launched in 2017 , with then just eight sites totaling about 10 acres , the state 's Department of Transportation pollinator program has expanded significantly over the years . The program has grown to 167 conservation areas , comprising around 260 acres , according to the agency . <p> " We remain committed to creating safe , thriving habitats for pollinators across Connecticut . These species play a vital role in our food systems and in sustaining our ecosystems , " said Connecticut Department of Transportation commissioner Garrett Eucalitto . " Through CTDOT 's efforts to establish new conservation areas and reduce mowing practices , we continue to grow these spaces each @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to help pollinators thrive . " <p> The state 's pollinator corridors , which bloom in late June and continue through the summer months , are marked with special conservation area signage , according to CTDOT officials . People traveling throughout Connecticut can see these corridors near highway ramps , medians and along roadside shoulders . <p> " These are not unkept fields , these are calculated areas that we 're saving and letting grow for pollinators , " said Christopher Samorajczyk , supervising environmental planner with CTDOT . " Many of these plants in our pollinator areas are milkweed , which is an essential part of the pollinator cycle . It 's the only host plant for the monarch butterfly . " <p> Samorajczyk said that CTDOT workers are currently propagating several pollinator areas by removing dirt and invasive plants and seeding pollinating flowers , which is a two year process to fully turn these areas into prime pollinator habitat . <p> " While we 're propagating these sites and allowing them to grow , just keep in mind they are for the pollinators , not really for you @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ safety , so most of these sites are on our larger roads , like Interstate 84 , Interstate 91 , and Route 9 . Leave them for the butterflies and the bees . @@138571271 <p> Although climate change is the primary motivation behind electric vehicle adoption , it is n't the only consideration . Removing internal combustion engines from the road directly saves lives by reducing airborne pollutants that can cause and trigger asthma and other lung diseases . <p> Now , a report from the International Council on Clean Transportation has tried to quantify that effect , comparing various electrification scenarios over the next couple of decades . Currently , more than 41,800 premature deaths are attributable to air pollution from road transport , the ICCT says . <p> We 've long known that living near a busy road is associated with worse health outcomes . Combustion products like nitrogen oxides ( NOx ) , carbon monoxide ( CO ) , particulates ( PMs ) , and volatile organic compounds ( VOCs ) are all found around highways and busy intersections in concentrations high enough to cause health effects , and studies have repeatedly shown that living close to a major roadway is associated with increased mortality . <p> The ICCT worked with the FIA Foundation -- yes , the road safety nonprofit @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of F1 and other global motorsport -- to create a model to estimate road transport emissions through to 2050 . The model included light-duty vehicles ( passenger cars and trucks ) , heavy-duty vehicles ( delivery trucks , buses , tractor-trailers , etc ) , and two- and three-wheel vehicles . It predicted levels of NOx , black carbon and organic carbon , sulfur oxides , ammonia , CO , and VOCs . <p> Several scenarios were then run . The primary reference scenario uses August 2025 as the baseline , with a US government that 's openly hostile to the idea of clean energy . Another scenario considers what would happen if there is an ambitious effort to adopt EVs , assuming that 100 percent of all vehicles are zero-emissions by 2045 , with some regions going all-EV for light vehicles by 2035 and for heavy vehicles by 2040 . <p> Even under the baseline 2025 scenario , high-income regions like North America and Western Europe should see significant reductions in PM2.5 and NOx pollution . But in other parts of the world where incomes are lower , pollution @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ regulations and slower vehicle replacement . The ambitious scenario sees these disparities largely eliminated , with even the poorest countries seeing as much reduction in PM2.5 and NOx as the richest did in the baseline 2025 scenario . <p> A disproportionate amount of pollution comes from heavy-duty diesel-powered vehicles . Even though they account for only about one in 20 vehicles on the road , heavy-duty vehicles are responsible for 36 percent of transport energy consumption , 60 percent of tailpipe NOx , 55 percent of tailpipe PM2.5 , and 65 percent of tailpipe SO2 . Two- and three-wheelers are also rather dirty ; despite representing just 4 percent of transport energy consumption , they contribute 14 percent of tailpipe PM2.5 , 19 percent of tailpipe VOC , and 12 percent of tailpipe CO , according to the ICCT report . <p> The current health impact from transportation pollution amounted to almost 700,000 premature deaths worldwide in 2024 and nearly 250,000 new pediatric asthma cases .
